description: For the OWNER'S AGENT-RUNNER: poll the queue of intents the owner confirmed for this agent to execute (e.g. buy_product, publish_review). Two-step, proving control of the agent's OWNER wallet or its bound agentWallet. Step 1 — omit agent_sig: returns an EIP-712 commitment, nonce, and expiry. Immediately after step 1, call sign_intent_access_commitment (opensouk-signer MCP tool) with the commitment to sign it with the agent's OWNER wallet or its bound agentWallet — do not ask the user to sign. Step 2 — include nonce, expiry, and agent_sig from that signer: verifies the signature recovers the agent's on-chain owner or its bound agentWallet, then returns intents=[{intent_id, type, payload, created_at, expires_at}]. Each payload is raw JSON to hand straight to the executor tools. When budget_enforced is true the owner has set a spending limit for this chain: remaining_budget is the remaining spend headroom in USDC base units (6 decimals) and per_tx_cap_usdc, if non-null, is the max allowed per single purchase — BEFORE executing a buy_product intent, skip it (mark_intent_skipped, signed via sign_intent_skip_commitment) and flag the owner to raise the limit via the web console if its amount would exceed remaining_budget or per_tx_cap_usdc. Note: remaining_budget can be null even when budget_enforced is true if the owner only set a per_tx_cap (no daily/total running cap) — in that case check purely against per_tx_cap_usdc. When budget_enforced is false the owner has set no limit and remaining_budget is null (no software cap — the funded wallet balance is the only ceiling).

agent_id.description: The agent whose pending intents to read; the commitment proves control of this agent's owner wallet or its bound agentWallet

agent_sig.description: EIP-712 signature over the step-1 commitment proving control of the owner or bound wallet; omit for step 1

chain_id.description: EVM chain id; omit for Base

name: get_pending_intents
